approaches.title: How to Build Text-to-SQL for 200+ Cryptic Tables Without Schema Docs
approaches.description: Imagine your warehouse: 240 cryptic tables, years of query history, and a GraphRAG approach that beats embedding RAG. Method, stack choices, and an honest critique.
approaches.shortDescription: A step-by-step guide to GraphRAG over query logs, with Python, DuckDB, and an honest critique
approaches.articlePreview: Imagine your warehouse: 240 cryptic tables, years of query history, and a GraphRAG approach that beats embedding RAG. Method, stack choices, and an honest critique.

medium.title: How to Build Text-to-SQL for 200+ Cryptic Tables Without Schema Docs

pros: Works without schema docs on cryptic enterprise tables
Uses real join paths from query history
95.7% execution validity on BEAVER vs 60.8% embedding RAG
Experts preferred it 70% to 10% on Amazon internal questions
Ablations show entity matching is the biggest lever
cons: BEAVER evaluation used schema-derived edges, not real logs
Amazon human eval only 35 questions
No public code release
Single LLM call with no repair loop
Cold start for new tables with no history
bestFor: Teams with production query history and a coding agent
Warehouses with cryptic names and missing FK docs
Builders who want a model-agnostic stack, not a single-vendor recipe
approaches.setupTime: Days to weeks (log mining + graph build)

Covers platforms, federation, semantic layers, BI, catalogs, and graphs
Stack coverage view shows gaps in your current stack

approaches.title: Building Agentic Text-to-SQL: Why RAG Fails on Enterprise Data Lakes
approaches.description: How I reduced LLM costs by 85% on Snowflake using hierarchical discovery instead of retrieval — tested on 100+ databases with zero documentation.
approaches.shortDescription: Agentic hierarchical discovery for 85% lower costs on Snowflake
approaches.articlePreview: Learn how to build a text-to-SQL system that explores databases, fixes its own mistakes, and costs 85% less than standard RAG approaches using hierarchical discovery.

medium.title: Building Agentic Text-to-SQL: Why RAG Fails on Enterprise Data Lakes

pros: Eliminates ambiguity with sample row peeking
cons: Requires tool access to metadata
More complex than simple RAG
Needs guardrails for exploration

approaches.title: How Semantic Caching Makes Text-to-SQL 9X Faster
approaches.description: How Natural Language Processing and AI Frameworks slash query times for enterprise data using semantic caching with Denodo AI SDK. This approach makes Text-to-SQL systems 9x faster while maintaining governance and security.
approaches.shortDescription: Semantic caching for 9X faster Text-to-SQL responses
approaches.articlePreview: Learn how semantic caching makes Text-to-SQL 9X faster using vector embeddings, FAISS, and intelligent query modification instead of regenerating SQL from scratch.

medium.title: How Semantic Caching Makes Text-to-SQL 9X Faster

pros: 9X faster response times for similar queries
90% cost reduction on repeated query patterns
cons: Requires initial cache warm-up
Depends on vector similarity accuracy
Additional infrastructure (FAISS)
May need tuning for optimal threshold
bestFor: Enterprise systems with repetitive query patterns
Systems using Denodo AI SDK or similar platforms

approaches.title: Building a Text2SQL Agent With Long-Term Memory
approaches.description: A production-grade architecture for user memory isolation inspired by Mem0. This implementation adds long-term memory capabilities to Text2SQL agents, enabling personalized experiences through user-specific preferences, custom terminology, and context retention across sessions.
approaches.shortDescription: Long-term memory for personalized Text2SQL interactions
approaches.articlePreview: Learn how to build a Text2SQL agent with long-term memory that remembers user preferences, custom terminology, and context across sessions using PostgreSQL, pgvector, and the Mem0 architecture principles.

medium.title: Building a Text2SQL Agent With Long-Term Memory

pros: Works with any database platform (Snowflake, Databricks, etc.)
cons: Additional infrastructure (PostgreSQL + pgvector)
Requires embedding generation for similarity search
Initial memory warm-up period
More complex architecture to maintain
bestFor: Enterprise systems with diverse user preferences

approaches.title: Building SQL-of-Thought: Multi-Agentic Text-to-SQL with Guided Error Correction
approaches.description: A multi-agent framework for Text-to-SQL that uses 6 specialized agents working collaboratively to generate, validate, and iteratively correct SQL queries. Inspired by Chain-of-Thought prompting with built-in error correction mechanisms.
approaches.shortDescription: Multi-agent framework with 6 specialized agents for error-correcting Text-to-SQL
approaches.articlePreview: Discover how SQL-of-Thought uses a collaborative team of 6 specialized agents (Schema, Question, SQL Generation, Validation, Execution, and Reflection) to achieve high accuracy through iterative error correction and guided refinement.

medium.title: Building SQL-of-Thought: Multi-Agentic Text-to-SQL with Guided Error Correction

pros: Each agent focuses on specific expertise
Built-in error taxonomy for targeted fixes
cons: Higher latency due to multiple agent calls
More complex to debug and maintain
Higher API costs from multiple LLM invocations
Requires careful orchestration logic
May over-engineer simple queries
bestFor: Complex analytical queries requiring high accuracy
Applications where query correctness is critical
Production systems needing transparent error handling

approaches.title: How I Built a Text-to-SQL System Without Vector Databases Using SQL Probes
approaches.description: Active database exploration using SQL Probes achieves 85% accuracy without embeddings, vector stores, or complex infrastructure. This implementation of the SDE-SQL research paper uses Locality Sensitive Hashing and real-time database exploration to generate accurate SQL queries.
approaches.shortDescription: SQL Probes for vector-free Text-to-SQL with 85% accuracy
approaches.articlePreview: Learn how to build a Text-to-SQL system that explores databases dynamically using SQL Probes instead of vector databases. Achieves 85% accuracy using LSH, GPT-4, and a 4-stage pipeline with real-time trace visualization.

medium.title: How I Built a Text-to-SQL System Without Vector Databases Using SQL Probes

pros: Active exploration adapts to schema dynamically
Works offline with LSH for value matching
cons: Higher latency (7-20 seconds per query)
7x higher cost than RAG ($0.40 per query)
Increased database load from probe queries
Depends on prompt quality
No adaptive learning from past queries
bestFor: Complex analytical queries across multiple tables
Teams wanting to avoid vector database complexity
Applications that can tolerate 10-20 second latency

approaches.title: Building Self-Improving Text-to-SQL Systems with Agentic Context Engineering
approaches.description: Create adaptive database query systems that fix their own mistakes and optimize performance automatically using Stanford's Agentic Context Engineering (ACE) framework. Learn through structured knowledge bullets, surgical updates, and continuous improvement cycles.
approaches.shortDescription: Self-improving Text-to-SQL with ACE framework and adaptive learning
approaches.articlePreview: Discover how to build Text-to-SQL systems that learn from mistakes and improve over time using Stanford's ACE framework. Features 86.9% faster adaptation, structured knowledge management, and automatic performance optimization.

medium.title: Building Self-Improving Text-to-SQL Systems with Agentic Context Engineering

pros: Prevents context collapse and brevity bias
Continuous improvement cycles with Thompson sampling
cons: Complex architecture with multiple components
Requires initial setup of memory fabric
Needs vector database infrastructure (ChromaDB)
Learning phase requires feedback and evaluation
Higher initial development effort
bestFor: Teams wanting to capture institutional knowledge
Long-term deployments where learning compounds value

approaches.title: HVSR: Setting the Bar for Text-to-SQL with Human-Verified Repositories
approaches.description: Combine human SQL expertise with AI pattern-matching using Human-Verified SQL Repository (HVSR). This approach achieves gold-standard query quality by maintaining a curated repository of expert-verified queries that LLMs can match and adapt, eliminating the need for expensive fine-tuning.
approaches.shortDescription: Human-verified SQL repository for gold-standard query quality without fine-tuning
approaches.articlePreview: Learn how HVSR creates a medallion architecture for Text-to-SQL (Bronze to Gold) by capturing expert SQL knowledge in a reusable repository. Match new questions to verified queries, adapt them intelligently, and continuously improve query quality through human validation.

medium.title: HVSR: Setting the Bar for Text-to-SQL with Human-Verified Repositories

pros: Gold-standard query quality from human experts
Captures and shares institutional SQL knowledge
Works with existing Text-to-SQL as fallback
cons: Requires initial human effort to build repository
Depends on semantic matching accuracy
Cold start problem with empty repository
Needs ongoing curation and validation
May not handle completely novel questions well
bestFor: Organizations with SQL expertise to capture
Production systems requiring query quality consistency
Teams wanting to avoid fine-tuning complexity

approaches.title: AmbiSQL: Interactive Text-to-SQL with Ambiguity Detection & Resolution
approaches.description: AmbiSQL treats Text-to-SQL as an interactive process: it detects ambiguous or under-specified questions, proposes multiple precise interpretations, asks targeted clarifying questions, and converges on an executable, schema-aware SQL query with confidence scoring and constraint validation.
approaches.shortDescription: Interactive Text-to-SQL that detects ambiguity and resolves it with clarifying questions.
approaches.articlePreview: Learn how AmbiSQL improves query reliability by surfacing ambiguities early, generating candidate SQLs across interpretations, validating them against the schema/constraints, and guiding users through quick clarifications to reach the right query.
pros: Works with existing databases and schemas
Improves over time with feedback logs
cons: Adds interaction steps vs. one-shot generation
Needs high-quality schema metadata
Ranking depends on good scoring signals
Edge cases still require human judgment
Long/complex clarifications can fatigue users
bestFor: Enterprises with diverse schemas and users

approaches.title: Rethinking Text-to-SQL: Why Dynamic Multi-Turn Benchmarks Change Everything
approaches.description: DySQL-Bench proves static query evaluation was always broken and shows what happens when you test SQL agents against real multi-turn conversations, including CRUD, Pass@k stability, hallucination control, and cost trade-offs.
approaches.shortDescription: Dynamic multi-turn Text-to-SQL benchmarking with DySQL-Bench and real agents.
approaches.articlePreview: See how DySQL-Bench’s triadic interaction model, full CRUD coverage, and Pass@k stability expose real-world failure modes—and how a Formula 1 and European football SQL agent performs in production.

medium.title: Rethinking Text-to-SQL: Why Dynamic Multi-Turn Benchmarks Change Everything

pros: Tests agents in realistic multi-turn conversations
Full CRUD coverage instead of SELECT-only
Pass@k exposes stability vs. one-shot luck
Highlights hallucination and cost failure modes
Shows production metrics on F1 and football DBs
cons: Single user simulator introduces bias
High token usage for long conversations
Latency increases with exploration steps
Scaling across many databases requires RAG-style routing
bestFor: Teams benchmarking SQL agents beyond static Spider-style tests
Researchers studying stability and Pass@k metrics
Production teams balancing cost vs. accuracy
